patches.title: Load/save dialog: "(EMPTY)" becomes "(LIBER)"

patches.title: Upper-case labels keep Romanian letters (FRANȚA, ȚESĂTORIE)
patches.asm_after: one shared loop; strupr also maps 1Ch-1Fh, 60h to the Romanian capitals
patches.summary: The EXE upper-cases some labels itself with the C runtime strupr, which knows only a-z, so ă â î ș ț stay small or turn into other glyphs. strlwr, strupr and _fstrupr now share one loop, which frees room for a 5-letter table. Built by ro/tools/upcase_patch.py.
patches.caveat: Romanian only. The site spans 0x10316-0x1070A; only its first 60 and last 35 bytes change, the rest is checked as is.
patches.notes: Runtime segment 0D1Dh (file 0xF5D0); the table is read as CS:1136h. No MZ relocation in the site. tests/test_ro_patches.py runs all three routines on every byte value in a small 8086 interpreter.
patches.verified: QEMU 2026-09-29 and Florin in DOSBox-Daum 2026-09-29 (screenshots A:\AAADev\colonization\bugs), no crashes.

patches.title: Nation names: no empty "The" and extra space before "Olanda"
patches.summary: The nation-name builder (far routine at file 0x8074) adds LABELS "The" and a space before the name of nation 3, the Netherlands. "The" is empty in Romanian, so "din  Olanda" got two spaces. The branch now always skips that block, as it does for the other three nations.
patches.caveat: Romanian only; the English "The Netherlands" needs the block.
patches.notes: LABELS @MISC is 221 near pointers at DS:2DBAh (loader at 0x75221); "The" is index 36, DS:2E02h, read only at 0x807E. The skipped block also lower-cases "The" when the caller asks for it. No MZ relocation in the site.

The type table DS:96E8h (NAMES @FOUNDING) is read only here for entries 0-4; entry 5 (Independence) is read at 0x3BA30 and stays. patches.title: Hall of Fame: "din Franța liberă" instead of "din liberă Franța"
patches.asm_after: push Free, buf; strcat(nation); if free: space, strcat(Free)
patches.summary: The Hall of Fame line is "<title> <name> <of the> [<Free> ]<nation>". The tail is rebuilt in the same 68 bytes so that "Free" comes after the nation, with its space: "din Franța liberă". LABELS Free and the buffer are pushed first; the later calls take them from the stack.

patches.notes: LABELS Free is @MISC index 191, DS:2F38h, read here and at 0x39D67 only. The four far calls stay at the same addresses with the same segment word (181Fh); only their offsets and the bytes between them change. No MZ relocation in the site, and no jump from outside lands in it. si is the row index, set at 0x3B169 and kept by the calls (the old code tested [bp+si-0E6h] after two of them); the dropped imul recomputed the same value.

patches.notes: Function 0x39888 (saves si). The flag test needs a register that lives across two far calls: si holds the flag address. si is dead here: its two reads (0x39A50, 0x39C45) each follow its own write (0x399B7, 0x39C42), and no jump reaches them from past this site. It now takes its middle from NAMES.TXT @INDEPENDENT, lines 4-7 ("Coloniile Angliei" ... "Coloniile Olandei"), by jumping into the President path, which reads "Republica Quebec" from lines 0-3 the same way. Rebuilt in the same 106 bytes.
patches.caveat: Romanian only. Needs NAMES @INDEPENDENT lines 4-7 (ro/glossary/names.tsv, rows 113/+1..+4); the English NAMES.TXT has no such lines.

The President path's tail at 0x3B27E pushes "INDEPENDENT" and "NAMES", calls 181F:0422 (the NAMES line lands at DS:833Ch), strcats it with the resident strcat D1D:07A4 and jumps to 0x3AF94 with 4 bytes on the stack; the Leader path pushes nation + 4 first and jumps there. DS:833Ch cannot go through 181F:016E: that helper (4B:00E2) takes a text-heap string number, not a DS pointer (it walks n strings from the heap base at DS:2D42h), and no 181F thunk reaches a plain strcat. All five far calls keep their bytes (overlay fixups touch their segment words; two are now dead code). The only jump from outside into the site lands on its end (0x3B299 -> 0x3AF94). No MZ relocation in the site (overlay code). LABELS Colonies (DS:2E78h) is then read only by F8 (0x39940).

patches.notes: Function 0x34318 (tax raise, [bp+6] = message section, [bp+8] = rise). At 0x3458C si = goods*2 and ax = colony index. The %STRINGn slots are 64-byte buffers at DS:9CD2h + 64n (text expander 0x6EF5C), so %STRING3 is DS:9D92h. 181F:0416(n, far ptr) and 181F:0438(n, text-heap number) fill a slot; both already serve slot 4 elsewhere (0438 at 0x3DA10, 0x5D9E9). Slots 0-2 stay untouched: MERCANTILISM, shown by the same dialog, uses %STRING0/%STRING1. The strcpy call at 0x345A5 is jumped over and left as it is, with its segment word; the two 181F calls keep their addresses and segment words, only the offsets change. No MZ relocation in the site (overlay); no jump lands inside it.

patches.notes: Function 0x34318, after the player chose the Tea Party. The colony offset moves from si to di (di is not read again before the pop at 0x3471B), which frees the 5 bytes of mov bx,[bp-2]; shl bx,1: si still holds goods*2 from 0x3458E (MSC far calls keep si/di). The add sp,4 after the %STRING0 call becomes pop ax; pop ax (ax is not used). The three far calls keep their addresses and segment words. No MZ relocation in the site; no jump lands inside it.
patches.verified: QEMU 2026-10-01, same rig as ro-taxparty-split, after choosing the Tea Party: "Partida de cojoace de la Jamestown! … 90 tone de cojoace … marfa aceasta: cojoace. Negoțul cu cojoace în Londra …" (live-new/10-teaparty.png; old build: "Cojoace" capitalised, live-old/17-teaparty.png); the game goes on to the next messages in both. tests/test_ro_patches.py RoTeaPartyTests runs old and new in x86mini up to the TEAPARTY call: %STRING0/1/2 as before but lower case, stack balanced.

patches.title: Text expander: %string<n> gives the slot with its first letter in lower case ("încărcătură de bumbac")
patches.asm_before: mov [bp-2Eh],ax (never read); slot = n shl 6 + 9CD2h; strcat(out, slot); add sp,4; [bp+6] += 7; jmp 6F0E9h
patches.asm_after: call 6F6D9h (ro-lowerstr-cave: push where the slot text will start); slot = n shl 6 + 9CD2h; strcat(out, slot); pop cx; pop cx; pop bx; if [bx] in 'A'..'Z': or byte [bx],20h; jmp 6EFC8h ([bp+6] += 7; jmp 6F0E9h)
patches.summary: GAME.TXT may write %string0..%string4 (lower-case s) where a goods name stands mid-sentence: the game appends the slot as for %STRINGn, then lower-cases the first letter of what it appended if it is A-Z. %STRINGn is unchanged, and the slot itself keeps its capital, so "%string1 ... %STRING1" gives "bumbac ... Bumbac".
patches.caveat: Needs ro-lowerstr-cave: alone it calls into the start of an unused function. Romanian only. Use %string only on goods slots (check.py LOWER_OK); a colony or nation name would lose its capital too. Every NAMES @CARGO name starts with an ASCII capital.
patches.notes: Text expander 0x6EEEC (overlay 0x17, file base 0x6BE50; thunk 191F:0910). The game already matches "STRING" with strnicmp (0D1D:0CC2), so %string expanded like %STRING before this patch; at the match [bp+6] points at the 's'. The dead store at 0x6EF56 becomes the near call; the tail after strcat (0x6EF68) pops the two strcat arguments and the pointer the cave pushed, and joins the existing [bp+6] += 7 tail at 0x6EFC8. The strcat far call keeps its address and segment word. Overlay code: no MZ relocation; no jump lands inside the changed bytes.
patches.verified: QEMU 2026-10-01, play/test-lowerstr: CARGOREADY1 with the first slot written {%string1} and the second %STRING1, Boston cotton 90 -> 99 in a save copy: "încărcătură de bumbac, … Boston nu mai are loc pentru Bumbac" (live-new/13-t2.png); unpatched build: "Bumbac" both times (run-old/27-k26.png). Memory dumps with the overlay at 9324h and 9BFFh: the changed bytes load as in the file; only the strcat segment word (0x6EF66, unchanged by the patch) gets the overlay manager's +56Ah fixup. tests/test_ro_patches.py RoLowerStrTests runs old and new expander in x86mini.

patches.title: Text expander: helper for ro-lowerstr-expander (where the slot text will start)
patches.asm_before: nop (pad); enter 0Eh,0; ... (start of the function at 0x6F6DA, never reached)
patches.asm_after: bx = [bp+6]+6 (the digit); if byte [bx-6] has 20h (a lower-case 's'): bx = strlen end of out [bp+8]; pop cx; push bx; jmp cx
patches.summary: The 26 bytes that ro-lowerstr-expander calls. For %STRING it pushes a pointer to the digit (never A-Z, so nothing changes); for %string it pushes the end of the output, where strcat will put the slot. ax (the slot number) is kept.
patches.caveat: Only with ro-lowerstr-expander. It overwrites the pad byte and the first 25 bytes of the function at 0x6F6DA (overlay offset 0x388A), which static analysis finds unreachable: no path from any of the 40 overlay-0x17 thunk entries, no pointer to it, no indirect jump in the overlay.
patches.notes: Same code segment as the expander (near call). See ro-lowerstr-expander.
patches.verified: QEMU 2026-10-01, play/test-lowerstr: the 26 bytes load as in the file (overlay at 9324h and 9BFFh). On the unpatched build with EB FE (jmp $) at 0x6F6DA, 90 SPACE presses over three turn ends and about ten message boxes never hung, and the marker was in memory at the end; EB FE at the expander entry hung at once (control). A fixed-address breakpoint cannot prove this: the overlay moves during play.
